Maya (People Ops): Quick heads-up — starting Mon 2024-09-02 were launching a short pilot for Compassionate Travel & Care Stipends and temporary remote-work guidance while on approved leaves. Details below and link to the policy doc. :sparkles:

Maya (People Ops): Key points —
- Compassionate Travel Support: up to $500 reimbursement for one-way emergency travel for immediate family emergencies (flights, basic accommodation).
- Backup Care Stipend: up to $75/day for backup childcare or eldercare when parental leave or short-term caregiver leave overlaps with work obligations, capped at $500 per event.
- Remote Work While on Leave: in special circumstances well allow intermittent remote work (max 2 weeks total during a single leave) with prior manager + People Ops sign-off.
- International travel pre-clearance: any travel >72 hours during leave or sabbatical requires pre-clearance via the travel form (link in doc) and may require security/travel safety sign-off.
- Expense process: submit receipts to Finance under expense type `compassionate-travel` and tag `people-ops`. Finance will fast-track these within 7 business days.

PeopleOpsBot: New policy published: https://intranet.redwood.ai/policies/compassionate-care-travel (summary + form). Effective: 2024-09-02.

Jonas (HRBP): Nice — thanks Maya. Quick q: does the backup care stipend apply if someone is on part-time leave?

Maya (People Ops): Good call. Yes, applies to full or partial leaves that are 2+ weeks, and to short caregiver leaves (3-14 days). Manager confirmation required.

Priya (Eng, SRE): For people on Dedicated support rotations, will approved intermittent remote work break on-call rules?

Maya (People Ops): If intermittent remote work overlaps on-call, teams need to arrange coverage; intermittent remote work is not automatic on-call exemption. Please coordinate with your manager and oncall lead.

Liam (Manager): How do we record the two-week remote-work allowance so its auditable?

Devon (Finance): Weve added a checkbox in the expense form and a small tag in HRIS. Managers should record approvals in the one-pager form attached to the travel/leave request.

Priya (Eng, SRE): Any guidance on visa/passport renewal costs if someones stuck abroad due to family emergency?

Maya (People Ops): Visa/passport emergency renewals can be considered on a case-by-case basis. Please raise with People Ops and include receipts + a brief justification; we'll route to Exec approval if over $500.

Jonas (HRBP): Will this affect PTO accruals?

Maya (People Ops): Accruals during paid leaves remain unchanged. For unpaid leaves, accrual follows existing policy (see HRIS -> Leaves).

Priya (Eng, SRE): Example submission snippet for receipts?

Devon (Finance): `expense_type: compassionate-travel`
`amount: 420.30`
`receipt: attached_pdf`
`note: emergency flight for immediate family illness`
`tags: people-ops, urgent`

Maya (People Ops): If anyone wants a runtime Q&A session, I can host a 20-min drop-in this Friday 1pm PT. RSVP on the calendar invite Ill send. :calendar:

Liam (Manager): Thanks — can you also confirm the expected turnaround for approvals? Managers + People Ops should respond within 3 business days?

Maya (People Ops): Correct — were aiming for 3 business days on approvals and 7 business days for Finance reimbursements. If its urgent (medical/emergency), mark as `urgent` and ping People Ops. :ambulance:

Priya (Eng, SRE): Thanks — appreciate the clarification.

PeopleOpsBot: Reminder: policy FAQ and pre-clearance form -> https://intranet.redwood.ai/forms/compassionate-travel-preclear (auto-closed in 60 days for pilot).

Maya (People Ops): Thanks everyone. If youve got edge cases, DM me or use the `#people-ops` thread.

Devon (Finance): Noted. Well add the new GL code and fast-track rule today.

Jonas (HRBP): +1. Appreciate the pilot and the quick turnaround plan. :thumbsup:
